cause_evidence: WHAT THE STORE SHOWS. 135 of the 144 off dates carry a straight-line interpolated price (source linear_interpolation); 9 carry a stored observed price (source transaction_observed). The three deep stretches (2022-08-01 to 2022-08-30, 2022-10-06 to 2022-10-28, 2024-04-02 to 2024-04-17; 51 of the 144 dates, ratio 0.1823 to 0.9657) are V-shaped ramps: the price falls in a straight line from an ordinary observed anchor (10.1185 on 2022-07-29, 9.4205 on 2022-10-05, 9.5504 on 2024-04-01) to one observed anchor far below the fund's price (1.8232 on 2022-08-11, 5.2299 on 2022-10-12, 5.2500 on 2024-04-04) and back up in a straight line to the next ordinary anchor (9.9104 on 2022-08-31, 9.2390 on 2022-10-31, 9.3100 on 2024-04-18). Four moderate stretches (2023-04, 2023-07, 2023-08, 2024-06; 59 of 144 dates, ratio 0.9134 to 0.9795) have the same shape on anchors 8.9109, 8.7044, 8.6335 and 9.0721 against a fetched close of 9.4 to 9.8. The 13 marginal stretches (34 dates, ratio 0.9756 to 1.0326) are within 3.3 percent of the fetched close, mostly a few days at about 1.02 or 0.98. NOT A UNIT: the six low anchors' ratios to the fetched close are 0.1823, 0.5605, 0.5526, 0.9139, 0.9134, 0.9146, six different numbers and not a power of ten. NOT A SHARE-CLASS PRICE: the sibling ETF class (ticker BND) is 7.5 to 7.6 times the fetched VBTLX close on every one of the 1,478 shared dates that have a BND price, so a class swap would put the build above the fetched close, not at 0.18; on the off dates the build VBTLX over the build BND ranges 0.024 to 0.136 against about 0.132 on ordinary dates, with no constant. NOT A SHARE-CLASS CHANGE: one CUSIP carries the symbol VBTLX and the description Admiral Shares in all 909 custodian rows, with no hand-over date, and no other CUSIP carries the ticker. NOT NAMED AS A WRONG SYMBOL: the price key is the ticker VBTLX itself and no other key or store supplies a price for it; but no custodian row prices VBTLX in 2018-2024 at all (the 909 rows are 2016-07 to 2017-01 and 2025-05 to 2025-07), so the 120 stored observed anchors from 2020-07 to 2026-06 cannot be traced to a custodian row. A search of all 1,416,497 custodian rows for a price within 0.0006 of each of the six low anchors, within 20 days of its date, found one set only: EIBIX in-kind contribution prints of about 5.2299 on 2022-10-11 and 2022-10-14 beside the 2022-10-12 anchor, while EIBIX buy and sell prints on those days are 4.74 to 4.79; no row matched the other five. That is a lead, not a match. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the silver price builder's input row for ticker VBTLX on each of 2022-08-11, 2022-10-12, 2023-04-11, 2023-07-03, 2023-08-02 and 2024-04-04 (which security, symbol and CUSIP the observed price was taken from, and the trade or reinvestment line behind it). Another security's price under the key VBTLX would be wrong_symbol_behind_the_security; a part-share or per-dollar scaling would be unit; a genuine low print would show a custodian trade of VBTLX at that price. Those rows are not in the local transaction cache and nothing was fetched. WHICH SIDE: no stretch has a custodian price in it (0 of 20). The only custodian prices in the shared window are on 3 dates (2025-05-30 9.5600, 2025-06-30 9.6801, 2025-07-24 9.5978), none in a stretch, the nearest stretch ending 56 days before; there the custodian price equals the fetched close (9.56, 9.68, 9.60) to 0.03 percent and the build is 0.5 to 1.3 percent below it. The custodian evidence supports the fetched close on 3 ordinary dates and says nothing on the off dates. THE REST OF THE SERIES: on the 1,338 dates that are not off, the build's close is the fetched unadjusted close, not the adjusted one. On the 111 of them carrying an observed anchor the median absolute difference is 0.009 percent and 89 percent are within 0.5 percent; on all 1,338 the ratio runs 0.9837 to 1.0181 between the 1st and 99th percentile with a median of 0.9997, 62 percent within 0.5 percent (the rest are interpolated dates between sparse anchors); the build is within 0.5 percent of the adjusted close on 0.3 percent of them. The round-74 reading looks unadjusted is right for the rest of the series. The r34 before and after files hold the same close on all 1,482 dates, so the anomaly is in both.
headline: VBTLX: 144 of 1,482 shared dates (9.7 percent) are off by more than 2 percent, in 20 stretches. The lowest ratio, 0.1823, is one stored price of 1.8232 on 2022-08-11 that the build joins to its neighbours by straight lines, giving a 22-date V-shaped ramp; two more like it (2022-10, 2024-04) and four milder (2023-2024) follow the same pattern. The cause is not named: it is not a unit, not a share-class price (the ETF class is 7.5 times higher), not a share-class change (one CUSIP, one symbol, one description), and a wrong symbol behind the key could not be shown because the source rows of the six low anchors are not in the custodian cache. Which side is wrong is not established: no custodian price lies in any of the 20 stretches. Nothing rests on the off dates: no account holds the fund on any of them (0 priced, 0 measured account-days); its 38 priced account-days are all 2025-05-29 to 2025-07-23, off none. Away from the off stretches the build equals the fetched unadjusted close. Round 70 classed it AGREES on its 2025 custodian prints. It stays excluded from every count.
not_established: Which side is wrong in any of the 20 stretches: no custodian trade or reinvestment price in or within 56 days of any stretch; custodian prices exist only 2016-07 to 2017-01 and 2025-05 to 2025-07.

The source of the 120 stored observed anchors for VBTLX in 2020-07 to 2026-06, and above all of the six low ones (1.8232, 5.2299, 5.2500, 8.9109, 8.7044, 8.6335): the local transaction cache holds no VBTLX row between 2018 and 2024. The builder's input rows for those dates are what would settle the cause.

Whether the 13 marginal stretches (34 dates, within 3.3 percent) are interpolation drift between sparse anchors or a real difference between the stored price and the vendor close; they carry no custodian price either.

Round 70's AGREES rests on 2025 custodian prints (dates outside every stretch) and says nothing about the stretches; the scan CSV lists only the 8 mis-scaled series, and VBTLX appears only in the detail file's list of securities that left the too-few class as AGREES.
Whether a sibling share-class price on disk would settle it: none was fetched; BND is priced by the build and its price does not explain the VBTLX levels.
Disclosure: one scratch query of this worker printed the VBTLX and sibling CUSIPs to the worker's own terminal; none is in any written file.
